summary_points: Document details: Client - Arizona Solar One, Project - HEX replacement TES Solana, Document code - 4521-MOM-LOI-039-062-0004-GAR
Prepared by Jon Ander Agundez, reviewed and approved by Iñaki Ugarte and Aitor López de Subijana
Important safety instructions include removing orange-painted parts, checking tightness of plugs, notifying LOINTEK for warranty work, and cautioning personnel around vessels filled with nitrogen gas
Table of contents includes sections on shipping/installation, start-up/operation, maintenance/reparations, and appendices
Caution section warns against removing covers or connections without proper venting and draining to prevent injury or death
Oil to Salt Heat Exchangers shipped with nitrogen gas for shipping and must be inspected for damage upon arrival.
Heaters should be stored on cribbing and not in contact with the ground.
Nitrogen blanketed heaters need regular pressure checks and maintenance.
Installation requires proper rigging and adherence to safety guidelines.
Two hook lift method allows vessel tilting for easier movement through tight spaces.
Remove shipping covers immediately before connections using grinding.
Bleed internal nitrogen pressure to zero before cutting off a cover.
Initial cold start-up involves filling with preheated HTF at a maximum ramp of 90ºF/hour (50ºC/hour).
Warm start-up follows normal charge or discharge modes, limited by temperature fluctuations.
Ensure system is clean and free of foreign objects before operation.
Do not expose internals to moisture or harmful contaminants.
Use nitrogen for corrosion protection until piping installation is complete.
Heater performance deviations should be reported immediately to LOINTEK.
Oil to Salt Heat Exchanger Systems are pressure tested according to ASME Code and PED 97/23 Directive.
Shutdown procedure involves stopping hot fluid first, then cold side flow.
Drain process starts with Salts, avoiding sudden shifts during removal or insertion.
Welding must be certified and reviewed by a Notified Body.
Shell removal requires careful support to prevent damage.
Reinstallation of the shell should ensure alignment and cleanliness.
Interference can be permitted during installation.
Fit-up lugs may be tack welded to the shell.
Radiographic examination is required on thick carbon steel seams.
Bolted connections should be tightened uniformly in a staggered pattern.
Gasket selection and inspection are crucial for proper sealing.
The document provides instructions on locating tube failures in Oil to Salt Heat Exchangers.
Visual inspection and penetrant testing are recommended for identifying tube failures.
Plugging procedures include different categories based on the nature of the failure.
General precautions when using welded plugs include cleaning and proper heat treatment.
Tests for plugged tubes involve bubble leak tests, penetrant examinations, and hydrostatic tests.
Pass partition cover plates can be removed and replaced with specific steps to ensure safety.
Document contains required documentation, hydrostatic testing instructions, and maintenance inspection points.
Hydrostatic test pressures must not exceed those stated on the nameplate and General Arrangement drawing.
Maintenance includes visual checks, retightening bolts, lubrication, and predictive maintenance.
Project is SOLANA with a revision date of 23/11/2016.
